figures.finding: From seven to eighteen a minor has limited legal capacity, and his declaration of intent (a contract among them) is valid only with his statutory representative's consent, unless it brings him only a benefit; marriage before eighteen gives full capacity. No earnings set-aside rule was found in the Civil Code text read; the Labour Code's rules on minors' employment contracts were not read (matsne refuses).
figures.applies: Georgia (Civil Code arts 12, 14, 15, in the WIPO Lex translation of the 1997 text; later amendments not checked).

sources.said: A person of the age of majority – an adult – is one who has attained the age of eighteen years. … A minor from the age of seven to eighteen years is a person with limited legal capacity. … A valid declaration of intent by a person with limited legal capacity is subject to the consent of his statutory representative, except when the person of limited legal capacity would acquire a benefit from the transaction.

figures.finding: A person may enter an employment agreement on their own from 16; under 16 only with the consent of a legal representative or the custody and guardianship authority, where the work does not go against the minor's interests, development or compulsory schooling; under 14 only for activities in sport, art and culture or work in advertising. The Code defines no light work.

value.law: Labour Code of Georgia (2010) art. 10; renumbered art. 4 in the 2020 Organic Law (not read)

sources.said: Article 10 of the Labour Code of Georgia specifies that the legal capacity of natural persons to enter into an employment agreement shall commence from the age of 16. ... Light work specifically is not mentionned in the Labour Code.

figures.finding: A child under 14 may be employed only in sport, art, culture or advertising, and any minor under 16 works only with the consent of a legal representative or the custody and guardianship authority, which once given holds for similar later work; the consent fails where the work harms the minor's interests, moral, physical or mental development or compulsory schooling. Hours, schooling arrangements and any lower age were not found, and the rule speaks of employment agreements generally, so it reaches a young writer or director employed in art or culture as much as a performer (reading).

sources.said: 'The legal capacity of minors under the age 16 to enter into an employment agreement 'shall derive from the consent of their legal representative or a custody/guardianship authority, unless the labour relations in question are contrary to the minor's interests, or prejudice their moral, physical and mental development, or limit their right and opportunity to acquire compulsory primary and basic education. Where the consent of a minor's legal representative or custody/guardianship authority validly constitutes legal capacity to enter into an employment agreement, such consent shall be valid with respect to similar types of subsequent labour relations as well'. ... 'an employment agreement with minors under the age of 14 may be concluded solely for the performance of activities in the fields of sport, art, and culture, and/or to do work in advertising'
